text: {"score":2,"justification":"The core numbers match the card, and the next steps and example claims are reasonable. However, the narrative makes several claims the card does not support, and some of them contradict the card. An investigator would be misled on parts of the picture.","problems":["Headline says 99215 is above expectation \"in every complexity band\", but the 0 and 1 condition bands are 4.2% and 4.0% against all-provider shares of 2.6% and 3.8%. The 1-condition gap is marginal, so \"well above\" is overstated.","The \"time-repeat signal (about 17% of notes)\" appears nowhere on the card or in the stated numbers. The number check passed, but the claim looks fabricated or unsupported. Note checks list only problems 3%, late 0%, unsigned 0%, data 0%.","Says \"Some low-complexity 99215s were documented as high MDM (for example C0043372)\". Only one low-complexity claim is cited, and the card shows C0043372 as a 1-condition (obesity) claim, so \"some\" is overreach.","The summary says the documentation is \"reassuring\" and the headline says charts \"mostly support the billed level\". That is thin: only 9 documented 99215 claims, with 4 listed as supported. The rationale also treats 0% below-billed in the other codes as comparable evidence.","Next step says to prioritize 2–3 condition patients, but no example claims with 2–3 conditions are cited. The cited low-complexity examples are for 0–1 condition patients, which is internally inconsistent with that focus.","The rationale reads as repetitive and contradictory. It says \"The excess is not explained by panel mix\", then calls the evidence inconclusive and reassuring. The \"leaning\" is inconclusive, which is defensible, but the text is muddled.","\"Against 17% for comparison providers\" matches the card, but the summary does not mention that the one below-billed claim (C0043026) is an example of weak documentation with no minutes."]}
